screenplay.text:
THE NIGHT TAXI

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

         1     EXT. BREE STREET TAXI RANK - NIGHT                      1

               Rows of white minibus taxis under orange floodlights.
               Engines idle. A vendor packs away a tray of oranges.

               BONGANI (50s), grey beard, flat cap, leans against a taxi
               with a dented front bumper. A string of plastic flowers
               hangs from its mirror. He counts coins into a tin.

               A boy in a too-big school blazer, THABO (9), stands alone by
               the queue barrier. He holds a crumpled piece of paper in
               both hands.

                                     BONGANI
                         You are waiting for somebody?

                                     THABO
                         My uncle. He said nine o'clock.

               Bongani checks his wristwatch. It is twenty past ten.

                                     BONGANI
                         Where does your uncle stay?

               Thabo holds up the paper. Bongani reads it under the
               floodlight.

                                     BONGANI
                         Orlando East. That is my last trip,
                         as it happens.

                                     THABO
                         I don't have money for the taxi.

                                     BONGANI
                               (folding the paper)
                         Then tonight the taxi is free. Get
                         in the front. The front is for
                         important people.

         2     INT./EXT. BONGANI'S TAXI - MOVING - NIGHT               2

               The city slides past the windows: shuttered shops, a burning
               drum with men warming their hands, a billboard for washing
               powder.

               Thabo sits in the front seat, seatbelt pulled tight across
               his chest. On the dashboard, a small radio glows green.












                                                                       2.


                                     RADIO PRESENTER (V.O.)
                         And that was the last song before
                         midnight. Drive safely out there,
                         Soweto.

                                     BONGANI
                         What is in the bag?

               Thabo hugs a plastic shopping bag on his lap.

                                     THABO
                         A trophy. I came first in the
                         spelling. My uncle didn't come to
                         see.

                                     BONGANI
                         Spell something for me. Spell
                         "roundabout".

                                     THABO
                         R, O, U, N, D, A, B, O, U, T.

                                     BONGANI
                               (impressed)
                         Hayi. I have been driving round
                         them for thirty years and I can't
                         spell it.

               The taxi swings around a roundabout. Thabo laughs.

         3     EXT. ORLANDO EAST - STREET - NIGHT                      3

               A row of small matchbox houses. Most windows are dark. A dog
               barks somewhere.

               The taxi stops outside a house with a green gate. The porch
               light is off.

         4     INT./EXT. BONGANI'S TAXI - CONTINUOUS                   4

               Thabo stares at the dark house. He doesn't move.

                                     THABO
                         Maybe he is sleeping.

                                     BONGANI
                         Then we wake him up. That is what
                         uncles are for.

         5     EXT. HOUSE WITH THE GREEN GATE - CONTINUOUS             5

               Bongani knocks on the door. Nothing. He knocks again,
               harder.









                                                                       3.


               A light snaps on inside. The door opens on a chain. UNCLE
               SIZWE (30s), in a vest, squints out.

                                     UNCLE SIZWE
                         It's past ten. Who is it?

               Then he sees Thabo by the gate, holding the plastic bag.

                                     UNCLE SIZWE
                         Thabo? Oh no. Oh, Thabo. The prize-
                         giving was tonight?

                                     THABO
                         You said nine o'clock.

               Uncle Sizwe takes off the chain and comes out barefoot. He
               kneels in front of the boy.

                                     UNCLE SIZWE
                         I fell asleep in front of the
                         television. I am sorry. I am so
                         sorry.

               Thabo opens the bag and lifts out a small gold TROPHY.

                                     THABO
                         I came first.

                                     UNCLE SIZWE
                               (to Bongani)
                         How much do I owe you?

                                     BONGANI
                         Nothing. He paid me in spelling.

               Bongani tips his cap and walks back to the taxi.

         6     INT./EXT. BONGANI'S TAXI - MOVING - NIGHT               6

               Bongani drives alone now. He turns the radio up.

                                     BONGANI
                               (to himself)
                         R, O, U, N, D...

               He stops, frowns, and laughs at himself.

                                                            FADE OUT.

shots.rationale: Captures the dialogue exchange where Bongani questions Thabo's wait and checks his watch, focusing on their facial reactions.

shots.rationale: Tightens on Thabo as Bongani offers him a free ride, emphasizing the boy's reaction to the unexpected kindness.

shots.source: Bongani drives alone now. He turns the radio up.
